scope: Service plans, account management, shared admission, burst bandwidth and traffic overage enforcement
environment: Windows Go 1.26.10; dedicated MySQL 8.4 and Redis 7.4 through the Hyper-V test VM; Chromium against the embedded console

other_packages.status: All packages except cloud passed in this invocation; cloud passed in the subsequent complete run above.
other_packages.first_run_limitation: The cloud package reached the default ten-minute package timeout during a fixture login. That invocation exited 1 and is not recorded as a complete pass. The complete cloud package was rerun with a twenty-minute timeout and passed.

regression.frontend: 11 tests, TypeScript, Prettier and production Vite build passed

plan_and_account_checks: Unique default plan; default assignment, explicit unassignment and multiple users sharing one tenant policy.
Unassigned new accounts have no usable nodes, bandwidth, ports or websites; migrated accounts preserve their existing policy.
Role and tenant isolation, version conflicts and atomic plan propagation; legacy quota writes cannot override managed plans.
Cross-node TCP/UDP port totals, independent website totals, concurrent admissions, protocol transitions and retained reservations.
Removing a node removes runtime rules, client authority and bandwidth grants; the multi-edge network test closes existing flows.
Password changes revoke other sessions and retain the current session; usage summary includes all grants beyond the raw-list limit.
Burst validation, hidden-field normalization, finite traffic cycles, reject/throttle validation and shared overage bandwidth.
Unconsumed reservations do not trigger early throttling; spent credit and burst tokens are not replenished by renewals.
Editing an elapsed cycle settles the old cycle before applying the new schedule; changing plans preserves current consumption.

verified: A live TCP connection waits at the included-traffic boundary for cloud-authorized excess credit.
The same connection resumes at 8192 bit/s and records 8192 bytes of bidirectional traffic.
Reject mode closes existing connections and rejects new flows.
Cycle renewal restores the regular rate and included traffic.
The edge UDP boundary test accounts a packet across regular and excess credit and sends one complete datagram.
Create, edit, set default and assign a plan through the administrator console.
Configure 20 Mbps, burst to 50 Mbps for 10 seconds, 100 GiB every 30 days and 1 Mbps excess bandwidth; changes reach the user account.
Zero-allowance reject and throttle states are displayed; the test plan is restored to 100 GiB afterwards.
Create a user's TCP service and HTTP website; toggle the website and verify persisted configuration.
Website creation only offers nodes with the required HTTP/HTTPS listener and selects the sole available node.
Website entry and copy use the actual nonstandard public listener port, including :28080.
Account, dashboard, usage, service list and plan form inspected on desktop and at 390-pixel mobile width.
No page-level horizontal overflow. Mobile cards retain equal left and right margins in viewport screenshots.
browser.fixture_boundary: The browser website uses a verified-domain and listener-node fixture in the dedicated QA database. This browser flow verifies UI and persistence, not public DNS or live website forwarding; actual HTTP(S) forwarding is covered by system tests.
browser.screenshot_correction: Chromium full-page capture hid the classic scrollbar and clipped the reflowed right edge. Recapture reserves the scrollbar gutter for the screenshot; actual viewport geometry has complete card borders and equal margins. Dialog screenshots include the surrounding viewport.
